subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'A neem tree is not a living thing. It can't walk and it doesn't eat.' Find the mistake.
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Neem ka ped jeevit nahi hai. Woh chal nahi sakta aur khaata bhi nahi.' Galti pakdo.
answer: Trees are living: they grow, take in water and air, make their own food and make seeds and new plants. Living things don't have to walk.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why a parrot and a kingfisher have different beaks.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki tote aur kingfisher ki chonch alag-alag kyon hoti hai.
answer: Beak shape matches food: the parrot's strong hooked beak cracks nuts and seeds and bites fruit; the kingfisher's long pointed beak catches fish.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Quick memory check: what is special about a duck's feet, and what do they help it do?
prompt_hi: Chhota sa yaad karo: batakh ke pair mein kya khaas hai, aur usse kya madad milti hai?
answer: Webbed feet, which push water like paddles and help it swim.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put these in a food chain with arrows: frog, grass, snake, grasshopper.
prompt_hi: Inko teer (arrow) laga ke food chain mein lagao: mendhak, ghaas, saanp, tidda.
answer: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake

subject: evs
prompt_en: On a farm: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. Predict: if most of the frogs disappear, what happens to the grasshoppers and to the snakes?
prompt_hi: Ek khet mein: ghaas → tidda → mendhak → saanp. Guess karo: agar zyadatar mendhak gayab ho jaayein, toh tiddon ka kya hoga, aur saanpon ka?
answer: Grasshoppers increase because fewer frogs eat them (and they may eat more grass and crops); snakes decrease or go hungry because they have less food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two pots of the same sprouting moong seeds: one kept on a sunny windowsill, one inside a dark cupboard, both watered. Predict how each will look after a week.
prompt_hi: Moong ke ek jaise ankurit beej do gamle mein: ek dhoop wali khidki pe, ek andhere almari ke andar, dono ko paani milta hai. Guess karo, ek hafte baad dono kaise dikhenge?
answer: The one in the dark will be pale yellow, thin and weak (often long and floppy); the sunny one will be green and healthy. Plants need sunlight to make their food.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Farmers kill all the snakes near their fields. Predict what might happen to the rats, and to the farmers' grain.
prompt_hi: Kisaan apne kheton ke paas saare saanp maar dete hain. Guess karo, chuhon ka kya hoga aur kisaan ke anaaj ka?
answer: Rats increase because no snakes are eating them, and they eat more of the grain; so snakes actually help farmers.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Every food chain starts with a plant. Why?
prompt_hi: Har food chain paudhe se hi kyon shuru hoti hai?
answer: Plants make their own food from sunlight, water and air; animals cannot make food, so they eat plants or animals that ate plants.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a cow's teeth and a tiger's teeth. How does each match what the animal eats?
prompt_hi: Gaay ke daant aur sher ke daant ki tulna karo. Dono ke daant unke khaane se kaise milte hain?
answer: A cow has broad flat teeth for grinding grass; a tiger has sharp pointed teeth for gripping and tearing meat.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Make a food chain from a pond using: small fish, kingfisher, tiny water plants (algae), mosquito larvae.
prompt_hi: Talaab ki food chain banao: chhoti machhli, kingfisher, paani ke chhote paudhe (kaai), machhar ke laarva.
answer: tiny water plants (algae) → mosquito larvae → small fish → kingfisher

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bees seem small, and some people only think of them as insects that sting. What would happen to fruit trees and vegetable plants, and to us, if all the bees disappeared?
prompt_hi: Madhumakkhi chhoti si lagti hai, aur kuch log bas sochte hain ki woh kaat-ti hai. Agar saari madhumakkhiyan gayab ho jaayein, toh phal ke pedon, sabziyon aur humare saath kya hoga?
answer: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower (pollination), so without them many flowers would not turn into fruits and seeds; we would get fewer fruits and vegetables. Small animals matter.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Say this food chain in words using 'is eaten by': grass → deer → tiger.
prompt_hi: Is food chain ko 'ko ... khaata hai' ya 'is eaten by' lagakar shabdon mein bolo: ghaas → hiran → sher.
answer: Grass is eaten by the deer, and the deer is eaten by the tiger.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu drew: snake → frog → grasshopper → grass, and says 'the arrow means eats'. Fix Golu's chain.
prompt_hi: Golu ne banaya: saanp → mendhak → tidda → ghaas, aur kehta hai 'teer ka matlab hai khaata hai'. Golu ki chain theek karo.
answer: Arrows go from the food to the eater: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake. The arrow means 'is eaten by'.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why a farm needs plants, insects, frogs AND snakes, and where the plants get their food.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki khet ko paudhe, keede, mendhak AUR saanp, sabki zaroorat kyon hai, aur paudhon ko khaana kahan se milta hai.
answer: Plants make their own food using sunlight, water and air; insects eat plants, frogs eat insects, snakes eat frogs and rats; each keeps the others in balance, so removing one upsets the chain.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time, finish this chain: grass → grasshopper → ___ → snake.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar wali chain poori karo: ghaas → tidda → ___ → saanp.
answer: frog

subject: evs
prompt_en: What is a sacred grove?
prompt_hi: Sacred grove (pavitra van) kya hota hai?
answer: A patch of forest that a village protects and does not cut, often linked to a local deity; the plants and animals there are left safe.

subject: evs
prompt_en: A hill has two sides: one side has a thick sacred grove, the other side's trees were all cut. Predict: after heavy rain, which side loses more soil, and near which side will a spring keep flowing longer into the dry months?
prompt_hi: Ek pahaadi ke do taraf hain: ek taraf ghana sacred grove, doosri taraf saare ped kaat diye gaye. Guess karo: bhaari baarish ke baad kis taraf zyada mitti bahegi, aur kis taraf ka jharna sookhe mahino tak zyada der chalega?
answer: The bare side loses more soil because nothing holds it; the spring near the grove keeps flowing longer because roots hold the soil and help rainwater soak into the ground slowly.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two jars of stored wheat are kept for a few months: one with dry neem leaves mixed in, one without. Predict which jar will have fewer insects.
prompt_hi: Gehun ke do dibbe kuch mahino ke liye rakhe hain: ek mein sookhe neem ke patte mile hain, ek mein nahi. Guess karo kis dibbe mein keede kam honge?
answer: The jar with neem leaves; neem helps keep insects away.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why did the people in the Chipko movement hug trees?
prompt_hi: Chipko andolan mein log pedon se kyon chipak gaye the?
answer: To stop the trees from being cut: by holding the trees they stood between the axe and the tree, because the forest gave them fuel, fodder and water and held the soil.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare what a village gets from one mango tree that stands for 20 years with what it gets if the tree is cut down once for wood.
prompt_hi: Ek aam ka ped jo 20 saal khada rahe, aur wahi ped ek baar lakdi ke liye kaat diya jaaye: gaon ko dono mein kya-kya milta hai?
answer: Standing: fruit every year, shade, homes for birds and insects, soil held in place, cleaner air. Cut: wood only once. A standing tree usually gives far more.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bishnoi people protect blackbuck and khejri trees. Think of one thing your family or colony could do in the same spirit.
prompt_hi: Bishnoi log kaale hiran aur khejri ke pedon ki raksha karte hain. Isi soch se tumhari family ya colony kya kar sakti hai? Ek cheez batao.
answer: Any sensible protective action, e.g. not cutting trees, planting and caring for saplings, keeping water bowls for birds in summer, not plucking flowers in parks, saving water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In many old towns of Rajasthan people built stepwells (baoris) and stored rainwater. Why was that smart in a dry place, and how is it like rainwater harvesting today?
prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai purane shehron mein log baori (stepwell) banate the aur baarish ka paani jama karte the. Sookhi jagah mein ye samajhdaari kyon thi, aur aaj ke rainwater harvesting se ye kaise milta hai?
answer: Rain falls rarely there, so storing it gives water for the long dry months; today's rainwater harvesting also collects rain from roofs into tanks or into the ground for later.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at this timeline picture: about 300 years ago, Khejarli villagers stand up to save khejri trees; 1973, Chipko people hug trees; today, villages still protect sacred groves. Tell the story in your own words, in order.
prompt_hi: Ye timeline picture dekho: lagbhag 300 saal pehle Khejarli ke gaon wale khejri ke pedon ko bachaane khade hue; 1973 mein Chipko ke log pedon se chipke; aaj bhi gaon sacred grove bachaate hain. Apne shabdon mein kram se kahani sunao.
answer: Long ago the Bishnoi villagers of Khejarli stood up to protect khejri trees; in 1973 the Chipko people hugged trees to stop cutting; today villages still protect sacred groves. People have protected forests for a very long time.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Old ways like keeping neem in grain or storing rainwater are just superstitions. Science has nothing to learn from them.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Anaaj mein neem rakhna ya baarish ka paani jama karna, ye sab purane andhvishwas hain. Science inse kuch nahi seekh sakta.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Many traditional practices work for real reasons that science can explain (neem keeps insects away; stored rainwater gives water in dry months); we can learn from them and test them.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu what a sacred grove is and how it helps animals, plants and water.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki sacred grove kya hota hai aur woh jaanwaron, paudhon aur paani ki madad kaise karta hai.
answer: A sacred grove is forest a village protects and never cuts; animals and birds live there safely, many plants survive, roots hold the soil and water soaks in to keep springs flowing.

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: what did the people in the Chipko movement do, and why?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Chipko andolan mein logon ne kya kiya tha, aur kyon?
answer: They hugged trees to stop them from being cut down.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name a plant used for each: making rope, making a roof, making a basket.
prompt_hi: Har kaam ke liye ek paudha batao: rassi banane ke liye, chhat banane ke liye, tokri banane ke liye.
answer: Rope: jute or coconut coir. Roof: bamboo, palm leaves, thatch grass or wood. Basket: bamboo or cane.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Bury a piece of banana leaf and a piece of plastic plate in a pot of moist soil. Predict what each will look like after a month.
prompt_hi: Ek gamle ki geeli mitti mein kele ke patte ka tukda aur plastic plate ka tukda daba do. Guess karo, ek mahine baad dono kaise dikhenge?
answer: The banana leaf will have started to rot and break into the soil; the plastic will look almost the same.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Before we look around: predict how many things in your room came from plants, a few or lots? Now find three and tell me which plant each came from.
prompt_hi: Idhar-udhar dekhne se pehle guess karo: tumhare kamre mein kitni cheezein paudhon se aayi hain, thodi ya bahut saari? Ab 3 dhoondho aur batao kis paudhe se aayi.
answer: Usually lots: e.g. a wooden table or door (trees), cotton bedsheet or clothes (cotton plant), paper books (wood pulp), a jute mat (jute plant).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Why do many people in India use a neem twig (datun) to clean their teeth?
prompt_hi: India mein bahut log daant saaf karne ke liye neem ki datun kyon use karte hain?
answer: Chewing the twig makes a soft brush that scrubs the teeth, and neem has bitter substances that people have long used to help keep the mouth clean and fight germs.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare a banana-leaf plate and a plastic plate after a wedding feast. What happens to each after it is thrown away?
prompt_hi: Shaadi ki daawat ke baad kele ke patte ki plate aur plastic ki plate ki tulna karo. Phenkne ke baad dono ka kya hota hai?
answer: The banana leaf rots and mixes into the soil (or is eaten by cattle); the plastic plate stays for hundreds of years and pollutes soil and water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Look at your lunch thali: name each item and the plant or plant part it came from.
prompt_hi: Apni lunch ki thali dekho: har cheez ka naam batao aur woh kis paudhe ya paudhe ke kis hisse se aayi.
answer: e.g. roti: wheat seeds (grains); rice: rice seeds; dal: pulse seeds; aloo: potato, an underground stem; salt: not from a plant.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Think about a cricket match. Which things in it come from plants?
prompt_hi: Ek cricket match ke baare mein socho. Usme kaun-kaun si cheezein paudhon se aati hain?
answer: The bat (willow wood), the wooden stumps and bails, cotton clothes, the grass of the field, and the cork inside the ball (from cork tree bark).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Here is a picture of a plant with labels: root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit. For each part, name one food we eat from that part.
prompt_hi: Ek paudhe ki picture hai jisme likha hai: jad, tana, patta, phool, phal. Har hisse ke liye ek khaane ki cheez batao jo hum us hisse se khaate hain.
answer: Root: carrot. Stem: sugarcane. Leaf: spinach. Flower: cauliflower. Fruit: mango or tomato.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Golu says: 'All plants are natural, so any berry or leaf in the park is safe to eat.' What is the mistake, and what is the safe rule?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Saare paudhe natural hain, toh park ka koi bhi ber ya patta khaana safe hai.' Galti kya hai, aur safe rule kya hai?
answer: Some plants and berries are poisonous; 'natural' does not mean 'safe'. Never taste an unknown plant; always ask an adult first.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu four different ways we use plants, with one example each.
prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki hum paudhon ka chaar alag tareekon se kaise use karte hain, har ek ka ek example dekar.
answer: Food (wheat, dal, fruits), medicine (tulsi or neem in home remedies; quinine from cinchona), shelter (bamboo, wood, thatch) and craft or clothes (jute, cotton, cane).

subject: evs
prompt_en: From last time: name one plant used for medicine and one used to build a house.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek paudha jo dawai mein kaam aata hai, aur ek jo ghar banane mein.
answer: Medicine: tulsi, neem, haldi or cinchona. House: bamboo, wood or thatch grass.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your thali has roti, aloo sabzi and rice. Which food groups are missing or too small, and what could you add?
prompt_hi: Tumhari thali mein roti, aloo ki sabzi aur chawal hai. Kaunse food group missing ya kam hain, aur kya jod sakte ho?
answer: It is almost all energy food; body-building food is missing (add dal, curd or paneer) and protective food is too little (add a green vegetable, salad or fruit).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Chew a small piece of plain roti slowly for about a minute without swallowing. Predict first: will the taste change?
prompt_hi: Saadi roti ka chhota tukda bina nigle lagbhag ek minute dheere-dheere chabao. Pehle guess karo: kya swaad badlega?
answer: Yes, it starts to taste slightly sweet: saliva begins changing the starch in roti (an energy food) into sugar.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Predict: if a child eats only rice and potatoes every day for months, with no dal, milk, fruits or vegetables, will they stay healthy? What might happen?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar koi bachcha mahino tak roz sirf chawal aur aloo khaaye, dal, doodh, phal ya sabzi bilkul nahi, toh kya woh healthy rahega? Kya ho sakta hai?
answer: No: they would get energy but not enough body-building and protective food, so they may grow slowly, feel weak and fall sick more often.
